newsitem.title: USA: Ice Harbor, Wash. 111 MW generator restart fails.
newsitem.headline: Ice Harbor, Wash. 111 MW generator restart fails.

text.p: One of the six generating units at the 603 megawatt (MW) Ice Harbor Dam on the Snake River, near Pasco, Wash., failed during post-repair testing this week, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers said Wednesday.
The Corps, which operates most of the federal hydropower projects in the Pacific Northwest, had expected to return the 111 MW unit 5 to service in January.
Engineers are now due to inspect the unit over the next two weeks and assess the length of time for further repairs, the Corps' Portland, Ore., office said.

The delay is significant mainly because Ice Harbor is a key point for fish migration and operators prefer to run as much water as possbile through power turbines rather than spillways, which results in toxic levels of gas saturation, a Corps spokesman said.
Unit 5 first went out of service in May 1994. After extensive retrofitting, it failed in May 1996 and again this week, the Corps said.
